propositions: The tests overlay is currently selected only by glob-triggered file matching (applies_to: **/test_*.py, **/*_test.py, **/tests/**) and misses product code changes with no accompanying test files, allowing buggy declarations to merge with zero test coverage.

A pure-text content trigger must fire when a diff adds one or more declarations (function/method/class across Python, Go, Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript) in any changed file, provided that file does not match the tests globs and the declaration name is not simultaneously removed in the same file.

The detector operates on composed diff context (diff text plus changed-files list) and must skip docs/data extensions (.md, .json, .yaml, etc.), non-anonymous declarations only, and respect per-file provenance to handle file moves (delete-in-A + add-in-B).

Guard (vii) in code-review-tests.md must be narrowed so a coverage gap finding is blocking only when it concerns newly-introduced behaviour (lines appearing as ADDED in the diff) and names a concrete violating input (value/argument/call sequence stated in the finding).

The content_triggered_overlays function requires a new keyword-only changed_files parameter to enable path-based negative matching, and overlay_union must pass the step's changed-file list and update its description to name the declaration trigger.
No regression across existing code-review trigger, deletion-impact, and evaluation tests; registry.py must remain under the 800-line complexity baseline.
